title: Canonical induced polynomial-module presentation
statement: Let A be any commutative ring, n a natural number, R = MvPolynomial (Fin n) A, S = MvPolynomial (Fin (n+1)) A, and ρ = rename Fin.castSucc. For every S-module M, put L = Res_ρ M and E = Ext_ρ L [def-weil-module-base-change]. There are S-linear maps δ : E → E and π : E → M such that 0 → E → E → M → 0 is short exact [def-weil-pbc-exact-sequence]. No Tor bound, finiteness or domain hypothesis is required.

source.document: C. Weibel, An Introduction to Homological Algebra
source.place: Corollary 4.3.6 and Theorem 4.3.7, pp. 101–102; https://math.mit.edu/~hrm/palestine/weibel/04-homological_dimension.pdf; source read online, including the proof of sequence (*)

proof.text: Set x = X(last n). Define the S-linear endomorphism tM = x times identity on M, restrict it to an R-linear t on L, and construct δ = x times identity on E minus Ext_ρ(t). Define π as the actual extension-restriction adjunction counit. Its tensor formula is π(s tensor m) = s m.

Rotate the variables with finRotate(n+1), then apply MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv. The resulting ring isomorphism sends ρ to Polynomial.C and x to Polynomial.X. Check the coefficient and variable generators using ring-hom extensionality. Make this an R-linear equivalence and transport Polynomial.basisMonomials to the R-basis b_k = x^k of S. TensorProduct.equivFinsuppOfBasisLeft gives an R-linear coefficient isomorphism c from E to finitely supported sequences in L; c inverse sends single(k,m) to x^k tensor m.

On finitely supported sequences put D = shift by Nat.succ minus coefficientwise t, and V = Finsupp.lsum of t^k. Compute D(single(k,m)) = single(k+1,m)-single(k,t m), and V(single(k,m)) = t^k m. Prove D injective: if Dq=0 and q is nonzero, take k=max support(q); q(k+1)=0, so Dq(k+1)=q(k), contradicting q(k)≠0. This uses no nonzero-ring assumption.

Prove for every q that Dp=q-single(0,Vq) for some p. Use Finsupp.induction_linear: zero uses p=0 and addition adds witnesses. For single(0,m) take p=0. For single(k+1,m), add single(k,m) to the inductive correction for single(k,t m); the formula for D and t^(k+1)=t^k composed with t give the correction identity.

Check δ c inverse = c inverse D and π c inverse = V on single sequences, using ExtendScalars.smul_tmul, the definition of scalar extension on maps, and the counit formula; extend by Finsupp.induction_linear. VD=0 follows from the same single-sequence formula, so δπ=0. Injectivity of D proves δ mono. π(1 tensor m)=m proves π epi. For π(c inverse q)=0, the correction identity supplies p with Dp=q, hence c inverse p maps to c inverse q under δ. ModuleCat exactness then proves short exactness.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_polynomial_induced_presentation
    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] (n : ℕ)
    (M : ModuleCat.{u} (MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) A)) :
    let E := (extendScalars (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.castSucc).toRingHom).obj
      ((restrictScalars (MvPolynomial.rename Fin.castSucc).toRingHom).obj M)
    ∃ (δ : E ⟶ E) (π : E ⟶ M) (w : δ ≫ π = 0),
      (ShortComplex.mk δ π w).ShortExact
